summary.headline: ACME Solar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to INR954 crore and EBITDA 56% to INR831 crore, with BESS contributing INR226 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record revenue and EBITDA for Q1 FY27, with total revenue of INR954 crore (up 63% YoY), EBITDA of INR831 crore (up 56%) and PAT of INR235 crore (up 80%). Growth was attributed to a record CUF of 30.9%, BESS revenue and new renewable capacity. BESS commissioning reached about 3.62 GWh cumulative, and the BESS commissioning guidance was pulled forward to more than 10 GWh by FY27 from calendar 2027. Management also said it has locked in about INR1,400 crore of short-term BESS revenue for FY27 and addressed a fire at the ACME Suryodaya BESS site, attributing it to an AC cabling short circuit rather than the battery system.

financial_highlights.change: Lower due to charging power cost in opex

segments.name: Renewable energy (solar/FDRE)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin ~88-89% in Q1; ex-BESS EBITDA margin stated at ~91%, with seasonal range of 88-91% over recent quarters. Management cited repowering of existing plants as a margin support.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR226 crore in Q1 with ~82% EBITDA margin; cumulative commissioned capacity ~3.62 GWh (about 40% of India's cumulative commissioned BESS). Management cites an annual EBITDA-to-capex yield above 20%.

guidance_outlook: BESS commissioning target raised to more than 10 GWh by FY27 (earlier: 10 GWh by calendar 2027), roughly three quarters earlier.
Around 1.5 GW of contracted renewable capacity to be commissioned in FY27, subject to substation and transmission availability.
Full-year FY27 capex upgraded to approximately INR15,000-20,000 crore.
About INR1,400 crore of BESS revenue locked for FY27 on roughly 70-80% of the ~10 GWh target; management said it could be higher if more volume is contracted.
Management indicated a 2-3 year assumption of INR1,400 crore-plus BESS revenue is reasonable; BESS EBITDA margin expected within 2-5% of Q1 level (~82%).
Management said it may increase its 2030 target beyond 10 GWh, to be updated in coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio 8,070 MW, with about 20 GWh of battery storage; under-construction capacity 5,080 MW.
PPAs signed for 3,880 MW, including 600 MW of new FDRE and hybrid PPAs with SECI this quarter; about 1,200 MW still awaiting PPA signing.
Debt tied up for about 85% of PPA-signed portfolio; INR6,000 crore financing secured for 700 MW of under-construction FDRE projects.
Battery procurement: more than 15 GWh ordered (CATL, Hithium); around 90% of the 20 GWh battery requirement contracted, with orders placed where PPAs are signed.

BESS capex ~INR93 lakh per MW including transformer, IDC and EPC; management said it could rise 5-10% for future batches. More than $300 million hedged at roughly $89-93 per unit of USD exchange rate.
Battery operations: round-trip efficiency ~89%, depth of discharge ~93%, state of health above 99.9%, availability above 99%; operating at one cycle per day.
demand_pricing: India power demand grew 8.8% YoY in Q1 to 485 billion units; peak demand hit a record 271 GW and was near 270 GW in July.
Short-term BESS realisations cited at INR8-10/kWh (publicly available DEEP portal and HP-TAM bids), sometimes higher; contracts are typically under one year, with 6-9 months' lead time.
Open (merchant) BESS capacity is about 600 MWh; management aims for zero open capacity outside PPA by end-2026, though a 300 MW plant is still open.

SECI is consolidating bids and will only bid with firmer power-offtake commitments, reducing near-term bid volumes; management expects large FDRE, peak power, CFD and state bids to follow over 6-9 months.
Management sees the peak-power market growing toward 300-500 GWh, potentially 1 TWh in a positive case, driven by rooftop and KUSUM solar (duck-curve effect).
Competition from other BESS entrants (including Adani) is rising, but management argues merchant supply will remain limited and that the market is still new to state buyers.

qa_highlights.question: How much open or early BESS capacity will there be in FY27 and the next couple of years, and what are realisations on the INR1,400 crore short-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is contracting well above 10 GWh and realisations are INR8-10 per unit, depending on month and volume. Only ~600 MWh is open today, with a target of zero open capacity outside PPAs by end-2026. Management plans for 10-12 GWh to remain available for short-term markets each year over the next five years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the curtailment impact and what drove EBITDA growth ex-BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment was about 1% of revenue, only on state-based projects. EBITDA growth was attributed to CUF (30.9% vs 28.5%) and repowering of existing plants. Management is considering adding batteries to state projects to absorb surplus generation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,400 crore revenue sustainable for 2-3 years, given El Nino-driven pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the 10 GWh base supporting INR1,400 crore-plus for the next 2-3 years based on PPA and GNA timelines. Beyond that, it depends on market pricing and new PPAs. It said the market is still untapped by most discoms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core (ex-BESS) EBITDA margin and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-BESS margin was ~91% in Q1, with a seasonal range of 88-91%. Management expects FDRE projects may lift margins because their realisations are healthier than plain solar.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 6.28 INR/kWh PPA and the hybrid configuration changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The hybrid project was offered with 1 hour of battery, a change from the standard configuration. The other project at INR6.28 per unit has no change in configuration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for C&I and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has started hiring for data-centre opportunities but is focused on profitability. It intends to target CTU-connected C&I customers and will not dilute mid-to-high teen return targets.

risks_watch: Execution on BESS commissioning: cumulative ~3.62 GWh must reach more than 10 GWh by FY27, with about 20% of that capacity still uncontracted and dependent on supply chain and timing.

Revenue sustainability beyond 2-3 years: the INR1,400 crore short-term BESS book depends on El Nino-driven state demand, realisations of INR8-10 per unit, and new PPAs or bids as SECI bid volumes have fallen.

Grid and transmission dependence: 1.5 GW FY27 renewable commissioning is tied to substation and GNA availability (SJVN FDRE GNA around June 2027), with curtailment about 1% of revenue on state projects.
Rising BESS competition (Adani and other entrants) and possible pricing compression on merchant spreads; about 600 MWh still open with a 300 MW plant unallocated.
Capex and cost risk: FY27 capex raised to INR15,000-20,000 crore; BESS cost could rise 5-10% for future batches, with about $300 million hedged at roughly $89-93 per unit of USD exchange rate.

summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on BESS demand, pricing and the raised commissioning target, with repeated emphasis on the 10 GWh base and peak-power demand growth. Cautious or non-committal on post-FY27 pricing and volumes (management said it would confirm when deliveries are made), and on the timing of solar GNA and the fire root cause, which it described as already resolved.
